headings.text: Period Home In Harpenden Goes On Sale

restContentHtml:
Homebuyers who love the idea of living in a period property might be interested in a house that has just come on the market in the Hertfordshire town of Harpenden.

A six-bedroom property that dates back to the early 20th Century located on Sauncey Avenue has gone on sale for £1.9 million.

One of the main selling points of the house is its popular location on a corner plot situated close to the local schools, station and high street, Hertfordshire Advertiser revealed.

However, once people enter the building, they are likely to be blown away with how its period features have lovingly been restored, showing off its original charm and character.

Viewers will discover the property boasts an entrance hall, living room, dining area, utility room, family snug, cloakroom and large kitchen/breakfast space.

There is also a master bedroom with en suite and dressing room on the first floor, as well as three other bedrooms and one large family bathroom. Finally, the second floor has two more bedrooms, one with an en suite.

Among its desirable original features are wooden beams, timber flooring, a fireplace, and a Tudor-style façade.

When looking for a property, period features remains one of the most popular criteria for homebuyers. Indeed, a survey by discountflooringdepot.co.uk revealed original features was why more than half (51 per cent) of people prefer period properties to new-builds.

The findings, published in Buy Association, revealed 42 per cent of those who responded wanted original windows, while 40 per cent desired fireplaces, and 37 per cent loved real wooden floors or authentic tiles.

Homeowners looking to bring their period house back to life should consider complete restoration solutions. Find out more by getting in touch with us today.
